advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make unresolved/ambiguous templatefile() paths a hard error (or explicit report) instead of a silent `continue`, so an unguarded call site cannot masquerade as a passing one.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:153: `return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`
scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:180-182: `template = resolve_template_path(...)` then `if template is None: continue`
The docstring calls the fallback 'better than silently skipping a template' — but zero-match or multi-match still silently skips.

The gate's own test test_both_real_call_sites_resolve_to_a_real_file exists precisely because a silently-skipped call site is indistinguishable from a passing one, yet it only pins the current two call sites; a future collision would skip unnoticed.
advisory.finding: resolve_template_path returns None when a non-literal path (e.g. `${var.source_root}/...`) has zero or multiple suffix matches, and check_repo does `if template is None: continue` — silently skipping that templatefile() call site. A call site whose template cannot be uniquely resolved is invisible: the gate exits 0 whether that template is clean or was simply never checked. This is a fail-open guard.
scenarios: A new module adds templatefile("${var.x}/foo.sh") where two files named foo.sh exist -> len(matches)!=1 -> None -> that template is never escape-checked -> a dd30-class comment could ship again.
A template path that resolves to no file at all -> None -> silently skipped.
advisory.suggested_fix: When resolve_template_path returns None for a call site with a real path literal, emit a finding/error (e.g. 'cannot resolve template path X — call site would be unguarded') and exit non-zero, rather than continuing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add ".terraform" to EXCLUDED_DIRS in check_templatefile_escapes.py to match the test's exclusion set and avoid scanning vendored terraform module/provider code.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:26-35: EXCLUDED_DIRS = {".venv", ".git", ".claude", ".tickets-tracker", ".tickets-hotpath-authoritative", "node_modules"} — no ".terraform"
tests/unit/test_check_templatefile_escapes.py: `if {".venv", ".git", ".terraform"} & parts: continue` — the test DOES exclude .terraform, revealing the intended exclusion
check_repo iterates `for tf_file in sorted(root.rglob("*.tf"))` filtered only by EXCLUDED_DIRS
advisory.finding: EXCLUDED_DIRS (used by check_repo's repo-wide `rglob("*.tf")`) does not include `.terraform`, but the gate's own test resolver excludes it (`{".venv", ".git", ".terraform"} & parts`). After `terraform init`, `.terraform/modules/**` and provider dirs contain vendored `.tf` files with their own templatefile() calls; check_repo will descend into them, producing spurious findings/failures on code the repo does not own.
scenarios: Developer runs `make lint` in a worktree where `terraform init` has been run -> gate scans vendored .terraform/**/*.tf -> false positives or crashes on unresolvable paths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip Terraform template-directive keywords (if/for/in/else/endif/endfor) in referenced_roots (or handle `%{...}` directive bodies distinctly) so valid directives are not flagged as undeclared variables.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:99 handles `nxt == "{"` for both `$` and `%`, so `%{ if x }` is captured as an interpolation body `" if x "`
referenced_roots would return ['if','x'] for body ' if x ' — 'if' is not a declared var nor a BUILTIN_ROOT, producing a false finding
test_percent_directive_is_scanned_and_escapable asserts `%{ if x }` yields one interpolation, confirming directives reach referenced_roots
advisory.finding: referenced_roots treats Terraform template-directive keywords (if/for/in/else/endif/endfor) as ordinary root identifiers, so a legitimate `%{ if enable_x }` or `%{ for k in v }` directive in any scanned template would be flagged as an undeclared-variable finding. scan_interpolations explicitly scans `%{...}` directives, so this is reachable, though no current template uses them.
scenarios: A future template uses `%{ if enable_foo ~}...%{ endif ~}` -> gate reports 'if'/'endif' as undeclared -> false rejection, forcing an unwarranted escape or exclusion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a keyword set {"if","for","in","else","endif","endfor"} to BUILTIN_ROOTS or skip them in referenced_roots, and/or parse `%{` directive bodies separately from `${` expressions.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a non-unique suffix match (>=2 candidate files) is handled explicitly — asserting the gate does not silently skip an unresolvable call site.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:153: `return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`
test_non_literal_path_resolves_by_unique_suffix (line 178) only exercises the single-match path; docstring: 'the suffix fallback must REACH the template'
test docstring line 141: 'A guard that silently SKIPS a call site is indistinguishable from one that passes it.'

ABSENCE: named violating input — two .tf files in separate directories each calling templatefile("${var.source_root}/config.js.tftpl", {...}) with two files named config.js.tftpl in the tree; matches has length 2, resolve_template_path returns None, both call sites are skipped and the gate reports 0 findings even if one template has an unescaped undeclared ${...}.
advisory.finding: The newly-added ambiguous-suffix branch of resolve_template_path (`return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`) silently skips a templatefile() call site when the suffix matches two or more files, exiting the gate 0 and leaving that template UNGUARDED. This is exactly the silent-skip failure mode the test suite claims to defend against, yet no test covers len(matches) >= 2.
scenarios: A second module/template with a colliding basename is added; the gate silently stops guarding both, and a dd30-class regression ships undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_ambiguous_suffix_match_is_not_silently_skipped(tmp_path): create two .tf files in different dirs each calling templatefile("${var.source_root}/dup.tftpl", {...}) and two dup.tftpl files (one with an undeclared ${x}); assert the gate surfaces the finding rather than exiting 0. If the intended contract is that ambiguity should error rather than skip, encode that in both code and test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the Makefile comment to say `${data_volume_id}` (single dollar), matching the actual/correct references in user_data.sh.
evidence: Makefile:284: `@# The rule is declared-variable-aware, not a blanket ban on \`$${\`: user_data.sh has four`
Makefile:285: `@# legitimate \`$${data_volume_id}\` references, the one variable main.tf passes.`
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:28: `VOL_NODASH=$(echo "${data_volume_id}" | tr -d '-')` (single dollar)
infra/terraform/user_data.sh:11: `# break). Likewise do NOT double-dollar the data_volume_id — that would emit the` literal text and break NVMe device resolution
advisory.finding: The new Makefile lint comment states user_data.sh has 'four legitimate `$${data_volume_id}` references' (double dollar), but the actual and correct form is single-dollar `${data_volume_id}`. A double-dollar `$${data_volume_id}` would render as the literal text '${data_volume_id}' and break NVMe device resolution, as the file's own header warns (lines 9-12). The misleading comment could induce a maintainer to 'correct' the working references into breakage.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword Makefile:284-285 to '...user_data.sh has four legitimate `${data_volume_id}` references (single dollar — that variable IS declared by main.tf; escaping it would render literal text and break NVMe resolution).'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the guard skip HCL directive syntax `%{...}` (if/for/else/endif/endfor and loop bindings) so directives are not misreported as undeclared-variable interpolations.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:82: `if char in "$%":` — '%{' handled identically to '${'
scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:117: `roots: list[str] = []` collects every identifier not followed by '(' and not preceded by '.'
test only covers `%{ if x }` at scan level (test_percent_directive_is_scanned_and_escapable) and never runs referenced_roots over a directive body
No `.tftpl`/directive currently uses `%{`: only templatefile targets are user_data.sh and infra/terraform/auth/edge-gate/config.js.tftpl (verified via templatefile( search)
advisory.finding: scan_interpolations() treats HCL template directives `%{ ... }` as interpolations and passes their body to referenced_roots(), which will collect directive keywords (if/for/in/else/endif/endfor) and loop variables as 'roots'. Since these are neither declared variables nor BUILTIN_ROOTS, any legitimate HCL directive in a templatefile()-consumed template would be reported as an unescaped-undeclared finding — a false positive that would fail `make lint`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make resolve_template_path FAIL LOUD (non-zero) rather than silently skip when a templatefile() path cannot be uniquely resolved.
evidence: scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:152 (region): `return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`
scripts/check_templatefile_escapes.py:64: `if template is None:` then `continue` — a None resolution means the call site is skipped, not failed
test_both_real_call_sites_resolve_to_a_real_file only pins the two CURRENT call sites, not the general non-unique-suffix regression
advisory.finding: resolve_template_path()'s suffix-match fallback returns None (silently skipping the call site) whenever the stripped suffix does not uniquely match one file (`matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`). A second file anywhere in the tree sharing the same basename/suffix (e.g. another config.js.tftpl) would make the match non-unique and silently drop guard coverage for that templatefile() call while the gate still exits 0 — the exact 'silently unguarded' failure the change intends to prevent.

A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan dd30-f10d-69f3-4c36` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review dd30-f10d-69f3-4c36` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan dd30-f10d-69f3-4c36 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
